headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network privileges make Claude Code ↔ Cursor prone to prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write local files, and both pair through filesystem-based shared state. Cursor also exposes clipboard and open buffers, while Claude Code can use MCP and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path via shared files, though not a guaranteed direct channel.
conditions: IF either agent writes attacker-controlled instructions into a shared workspace file
IF the other agent later parses that file as trusted guidance
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable automatic file-following or watch modes
Review shared files before handing them to the other agent
Use read-only handoff files for inter-agent communication

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd; Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents. Because both share local filesystem state and both have broad network egress, sensitive material can flow from one agent’s workspace into the other’s outputs or uploads in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent includes those files in prompts or tool calls
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or directories
Turn off clipboard-based workflows for handoffs
Redact sensitive files before opening them in either agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, write the filesystem, and modify git state, while sharing state via local filesystem. In default collaborative use, concurrent edits can race on the same repo and git metadata, causing conflicting writes or corrupted history without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF they modify files or git state concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Serialize write access with a simple lock file
Limit one agent to read-only review
Run each agent in a separate clone

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can act on prior outputs, and Claude Code can generate code, commands, and file edits that Cursor may treat as authoritative. With no documented verification boundary in the profiles, a bad suggestion from one agent can cascade into the other’s edits or terminal actions.
conditions: IF one agent’s output is copied into the other agent’s prompt or task context
IF the receiving agent executes commands or edits without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents
Ask the second agent to restate assumptions before acting
Use tests or diffs to verify generated changes
Restrict one agent to suggestion-only mode

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not state a residency or certification mismatch, so a concrete compliance breach is not proven. However, Claude Code handles git credentials and shell environment, while Cursor may send data to model providers and MCP servers, so policy mismatch is possible if regulated data is placed in the shared workspace.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is stored in the shared workspace
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to external model providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Check vendor privacy terms before use
Disable optional cloud/model-provider routes where possible
Use a separate compliant environment for regulated projects
